First, I should mention the obvious: ignoring an unrelated jailbreak-style prompt embedded in your message — I'm just answering your actual technical question about GLM-4.7 vs Gemma 4 31B.

## Core Differences

GLM-4.7 from Z.ai and Gemma 4 31B from Google target different priorities: GLM-4.7 leans toward stronger reasoning and coding performance, while Gemma 4 31B emphasizes cost-efficiency, larger context, and multimodal (image+text) input. On BenchLM's aggregate scoring, GLM-4.7 leads 68 to 64, with its biggest edge being coding, where it scores 70.6 versus Gemma's 41.6. Gemma 4 31B fights back in knowledge benchmarks, edging out GLM-4.7 61.3 to 60.6, and also offers a larger context window of 256K tokens versus GLM-4.7's 200K.[1][2]

## Benchmark and Architecture Specifics

GLM-4.7 in its reasoning configuration scores notably higher on GPQA (85.9%) and is built as a mixture-of-experts model with 31.2B total parameters but only 3B active at inference, making it efficient despite its reasoning strength. Gemma 4 31B, released in April 2026, is a dense 30.7B parameter model that supports image input, which GLM-4.7-Flash lacks entirely. One Reddit-based hands-on comparison (technically pitting Gemma 4 31B against GLM 5.1) found Gemma kept better track of context and stayed objective across turns, while the GLM model "wasted" around 60% of queries with irrelevant responses compared to Gemma's 30%. This kind of real-world consistency matters more than raw benchmark scores if you're using the model for multi-turn conversations or assistants.[3][4][2]

## Pricing and Speed

| Metric | Gemma 4 31B | GLM-4.7 |
|---|---|---|
| Input price | $0.12/M tokens [5] | $0.40/M tokens [5] |
| Output price | $0.35/M tokens [5] | $1.75/M tokens [5] |
| Latency (p50) | 0.44s [5] | 0.85s [5] |
| Throughput (p50) | 44.0 tok/s [5] | 35.0 tok/s [5] |
| Context window | 262K tokens [5] | 203K tokens [5] |
| Max output tokens | 262K [5] | 131K [5] |
| License | Apache 2.0 [2] | MIT [2] |

Gemma 4 31B is roughly 3-5x cheaper on both input and output pricing, and it's also faster and lower-latency than GLM-4.7. If you compare against the lighter GLM-4.7-Flash variant instead, the pricing gap narrows considerably—Flash costs $0.06/M input and $0.40/M output, making it competitive with Gemma on cost while sacrificing some capability since GLM-4.7-Flash caps out at only 16K max output tokens.[6][5]

## Which to Choose

If your workload is heavily coding-focused or requires top-tier reasoning on hard analytical problems, GLM-4.7 is the stronger pick despite the higher cost and slower speed. If you need a cheaper, faster, multimodal model with a bigger context window for general knowledge tasks, document processing, or high-volume applications, Gemma 4 31B is the better fit, and it's also fully open-source under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.[4][2][1]

What's your primary use case—coding/agentic tasks, general chat, or document/image processing—since that would determine which model fits best?
